mission: Trace surviving radiocarbon-dated human bone from Djer Tomb O to its present museum custody and original micro-context, to distinguish Early Dynastic biological material from later Osirian cult deposits without identifying any individual as Djer or Osiris.

published_dataset_anchor.publication: Dee et al. 2013, Proceedings of the Royal Society A 469, 20130395, DOI 10.1098/rspa.2013.0395
published_dataset_anchor.institutional_context: The 2013 project included Natural History Museum London among collaborating institutions; co-author Linus Girdland Flink was affiliated with NHM. This does not by itself prove custody of the AF.11.4 samples.

numbering_control.known_parallel: BMNH AF.11.4/427 is a documented Natural History Museum London human-remains number for an Abydos First-Dynasty individual from the same broad Petrie collection family.
numbering_control.inference: AF.11.4.406/.409/.414 may belong to NHM London, but numbering-family similarity is not enough for a PASS.
numbering_control.required_pass: NHM catalogue/curatorial confirmation or original Dee-project sample table explicitly binding these sample numbers to NHM custody.

outreach.target: Dr Rachel Ives, Curator Anthropology, Natural History Museum London
outreach.request: Confirm custody/catalogue numbers, skeletal elements, individualization, original labels/micro-context, sampled element, existing analytical history, and any explicit relation or non-relation to the bracelet-bearing Tomb O forearm.

relation_to_lost_arm_gate.lost_arm: The famous bracelet-bearing forearm itself was discarded in Cairo; no direct radiocarbon measurement of that arm is known.
relation_to_lost_arm_gate.surviving_bones: These three bone records establish that other real human skeletal material attributed to Tomb O was sufficiently preserved to be radiocarbon dated in the modern period.
relation_to_lost_arm_gate.prohibited_join: Do not infer that AF.11.4.406/.409/.414 belonged to the lost forearm individual, King Djer, a queen, or Osiris without direct object-level evidence.

next_actions: Obtain NHM response or Dee-project supplementary sample table binding AF.11.4 numbers to an institution.
Recover original AF labels and Petrie Tomb O chamber map to spatially place .406, .409 and .414.
Determine whether Chamber 13 was an original subsidiary burial, later disturbed area, or later Osirian deposition context.
Compare biological sample dates and contexts with the Middle Kingdom-and-later Osiris-tomb reception phases.
Never merge the dated bone samples with the lost arm individual without a direct archival/osteological join.
canonical_formula: TOMB_O_HUMAN_BONE + C14 + MICROCONTEXT + CUSTODY -> PHASE_CLASSIFICATION; NEVER -> OSIRIS_IDENTITY
canonical_seal: THE LOST ARM IS NOT THE ONLY HUMAN BIOLOGY LEFT FROM TOMB O. THREE OTHER HUMAN-BONE RECORDS WERE RADIOCARBON DATED. NOW FIND THEIR BODIES, LABELS AND CHAMBERS—WITHOUT INVENTING THEIR NAMES.
